decisions.reason: As a digital patient workflow tool tightly connected to the firm's existing dental software knowledge and customer base, it fits high absorptive capacity and is likely worth further refinement rather than withdrawal.

Although continuing education is less central than software, it still builds on the firm's deep dental-practice knowledge and client relationships, so management would likely retain it as a complementary offering.
A remote screen-sharing support tool is closely related to the firm's installed software base and service routines, making it easy to understand, improve, and use commercially.
Practice analytics directly leverages the firm's knowledge of dental practice data and workflows, so absorptive capacity is high and the product is likely to be developed further.
A complete dental practice bundle is adjacent to the firm's core business and can exploit existing integration, sales, and customer knowledge, even if it is broader than a single software module.

A job and practice listing portal is the least connected to the firm's core programming and practice-management capabilities, so management is more likely to reallocate resources away from it if traction is uncertain.
